Large-scale DNA study maps 37,000 years of human disease history
Researchers have mapped the spread of infectious diseases in humans across millennia, to reveal how human-animal interactions permanently transformed our health today.
We’ve long suspected that the transition to farming and animal husbandry opened the door to a new era of disease – now DNA shows us that it happened at least 6,500 years ago
Eske Willerslev
A new study suggests that our ancestors’ close cohabitation with domesticated animals and large-scale migrations played a key role in the spread of infectious diseases.
The team, led by Professor Eske Willerslev at the Universities of Cambridge and Copenhagen, recovered ancient DNA from 214 known human pathogens in prehistoric humans from Eurasia.
They found that the earliest evidence of zoonotic diseases – illnesses transmitted from animals to humans, like COVID in recent times – dates back to around 6,500 years ago, with these diseases becoming more widespread approximately 5,000 years ago.
The study detected the world’s oldest genetic trace of the plague bacterium,
Yersinia pestis
, in a 5,500-year-old sample. The plague is estimated to have killed between one-quarter and one-half of Europe’s population during the Middle Ages.
In addition, the researchers found traces of many other diseases including:
Malaria (
Plasmodium vivax
) – 4,200 years ago
Leprosy (
Mycobacterium leprae
) – 1,400 years ago
Hepatitis B virus – 9,800 years ago
Diphtheria (
Corynebacterium diphtheriae
) – 11,100 years ago
This is the largest study to date on the history of infectious diseases and is
published today in the journal
Nature
.
The researchers analysed DNA from over 1,300 prehistoric humans, some up to 37,000 years old. The ancient bones and teeth have provided a unique insight into the development of diseases caused by bacteria, viruses, and parasites.
“We’ve long suspected that the transition to farming and animal husbandry opened the door to a new era of disease – now DNA shows us that it happened at least 6,500 years ago,” said Willerslev.
He added: “These infections didn’t just cause illness – they may have contributed to population collapse, migration, and genetic adaptation.”
The significant increase in the incidence of zoonoses around 5,000 years ago coincides with a migration to north-western Europe from the Pontic Steppe – that is from parts of present-day Ukraine, south-western Russia and western Kazakhstan. The people embarking on this migration – and who to a large extent passed on the genetic profile found among people in north-western Europe today – belonged to the Yamnaya herders.
The findings could be significant for the development of vaccines and for understanding how diseases arise and mutate over time.
“If we understand what happened in the past, it can help us prepare for the future. Many of the newly emerging infectious diseases are predicted to originate from animals,” said Associate Professor Martin Sikora at the University of Copenhagen, and first author of the report.
Willerslev added: “Mutations that were successful in the past are likely to reappear. This knowledge is important for future vaccines, as it allows us to test whether current vaccines provide sufficient coverage or whether new ones need to be developed due to mutations.”

Sam Altman, CEO of OpenAI, at the Hope Global Forums annual meeting in Atlanta on Dec. 11, 2023.
Dustin Chambers | Bloomberg | Getty Images
OpenAI
is close to releasing an AI-powered web browser that will challenge
Alphabet's
market-dominating Google Chrome, three people familiar with the matter told Reuters.
The browser is slated to launch in the coming weeks, three of the people said, and aims to use artificial intelligence to fundamentally change how consumers browse the web. It will give OpenAI more direct access to a cornerstone of Google's success: user data.
If adopted by the 400 million weekly active users of ChatGPT, OpenAI's browser could put pressure on a key component of rival Google's ad-money spigot. Chrome is an important pillar of Alphabet's ad business, which makes up nearly three-quarters of its revenue, as Chrome provides user information to help Alphabet target ads more effectively and profitably, and also gives Google a way to route search traffic to its own engine by default.
OpenAI's browser is designed to keep some user interactions within a ChatGPT-like native chat interface instead of clicking through to websites, two of the sources said.
The browser is part of a broader strategy by OpenAI to weave its services across the personal and work lives of consumers, one of the sources said.
OpenAI declined to comment.
The sources declined to be identified because they are not authorized to speak publicly on the matter.
Led by entrepreneur Sam Altman, OpenAI upended the tech industry with the launch of its AI chatbot ChatGPT in late 2022. After its initial success, OpenAI has faced stiff competition from rivals including Google and startup Anthropic, and is looking for new areas of growth.
In May, OpenAI said it would enter the hardware domain, paying $6.5 billion to buy io, an AI devices startup from Apple's former design chief, Jony Ive.
A web browser would allow OpenAI to directly integrate its AI agent products such as Operator into the browsing experience, enabling the browser to carry out tasks on behalf of the user, the people said.
The browser's access to a user's web activity would make it the ideal platform for AI "agents" that can take actions on their behalf, like booking reservations or filling out forms, directly within the websites they use.
Tough competition
OpenAI has its work cut out - Google Chrome, which is used by more than 3 billion people, currently holds more than two-thirds of the worldwide browser market, according to web analytics firm StatCounter. Apple's second-place Safari lags far behind with a 16% share. Last month, OpenAI said it had 3 million paying business users for ChatGPT.
Other AI startups like The Browser Company and Brave have announced AI-powered browsers capable of performing actions on a user's behalf this year. Perplexity, a well-funded startup known for its search engine, also launched its AI browser, Comet, on Wednesday.
Chrome's role in providing user information to help Alphabet target ads more effectively and profitably has proven so successful that the Department of Justice has demanded its divestiture after a U.S. judge last year ruled that the Google parent holds an unlawful monopoly in online search.
OpenAI's browser is built atop Chromium, Google's own open-source browser code, two of the sources said. Chromium is the source code for Google Chrome, as well as many competing browsers including Microsoft's Edge and Opera.
Last year, OpenAI hired two longtime Google vice presidents who were part of the original team that developed Google Chrome. The Information was first to report their hires and that OpenAI previously considered building a browser.
An OpenAI executive testified in April that the company would be interested in buying Chrome if antitrust enforcers succeeded in forcing the sale.
Google has not offered Chrome for sale. The company has said it plans to appeal the ruling that it holds a monopoly.
OpenAI decided to build its own browser, rather than simply a "plug-in" on top of another company's browser, in order to have more control over the data it can collect, one source said.

data.title: YouTube prepares crackdown on mass-produced videos as concern over AI slop grows
data.author: baylearn
data.article_summary: YouTube计划更新其政策，打击通过“非原创”内容获利的行为，包括批量制作和重复内容，这些内容在AI技术帮助下变得更容易生成。7月15日，YouTube将更新其合作伙伴计划（YPP）的 monetization 政策，提供更详细的指导，明确哪些内容可以盈利。尽管具体政策尚未公布，但YouTube强调创作者需上传“原创”和“真实”内容。一些创作者担心这会影响反应视频或包含剪辑的视频的盈利能力，但YouTube高管Rene Ritchie表示，这仅是“小更新”，旨在更好地识别批量生产或重复内容，且这类内容多年来一直无法盈利。随着AI技术发展，低质量的AI生成内容在YouTube上泛滥，包括AI语音和虚假新闻视频，甚至YouTube高管的形象也被用于AI诈骗。尽管YouTube称更新为“小调整”，但清除AI劣质内容对维护其声誉至关重要。

44520105.article_content:
YouTube is preparing to
update its policies
to crack down on creators’ ability to generate revenue from “inauthentic” content, including mass-produced videos and other types of repetitive content — things that have become easier to generate with the help of AI technology.
On July 15, the company will update its YouTube Partner Program (YPP) Monetization policies with more detailed guidelines around what type of content can earn creators money and what cannot.
The exact policy language itself has not yet been released, but a page on
YouTube’s Help documentation
explains that creators have always been required to upload “original” and “authentic” content. The update says that the new language will help creators to better understand what “inauthentic” content looks like today.
Some YouTube creators were concerned that the update would limit their ability to monetize certain types of videos, like reaction videos or those featuring clips, but a post from YouTube Head of Editorial & Creator Liaison Rene Ritchie says that’s not the case.
In a video update
published
on Tuesday, Ritchie says that the change is just a “minor update” to YouTube’s longstanding YPP policies and is designed to better identify when content is mass-produced or repetitive.
Plus, Ritchie adds, this type of content has been ineligible for monetization for years, as it’s content that viewers often consider spam.
What Ritchie is not saying, however, is how much easier it is to create such videos these days.
With the rise of AI technology, YouTube has become flooded with AI slop, a term referencing low-quality media or content made using generative AI technology. For
instance
, it’s
common
to
find
an AI voice overlaid on photos, video clips, or other repurposed content, thanks to text-to-video AI tools. Some channels filled with AI music have
millions
of subscribers. Fake, AI-generated videos about news events,
like the Diddy trial, have racked up millions of views
.
In another example, a true crime murder series on YouTube that went viral was found to be entirely AI-generated,
404 Media reported
earlier this year. Even YouTube CEO Neal Mohan’s
likeness was used
in an AI-generated phishing scam on the site, despite having tools in place that allow users
to report deepfake videos
.
While YouTube may downplay the coming changes as a “minor” update or clarification, the reality is that allowing this type of content to grow and its creators to profit could ultimately damage YouTube’s reputation and value. It’s no surprise, then, that the company wants clear policies in place that allow it to enact mass bans of AI slop creators from YPP.

data.title: Helm local code execution via a malicious chart
data.author: irke882
data.article_summary: 文章主要介绍了Helm中的一个高危安全漏洞（CVE-2025-53547）。在Helm版本≤3.18.3中，恶意构造的`Chart.yaml`文件和符号链接的`Chart.lock`文件可能导致本地代码执行。当用户运行`helm dependency update`时，某些字段会被带入`Chart.lock`文件，如果该文件被符号链接到可执行文件（如`bash.rc`或shell脚本），可能导致 unwanted 的代码执行。此问题已在Helm v3.18.4中修复。作为临时解决方案，用户应确保`Chart.lock`文件不是符号链接。漏洞的CVSS评分为8.5，属于高危级别。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Helm图表依赖更新过程中存在的安全漏洞及其潜在的攻击向量和影响

不同观点：
• [yelirekim] 详细解释了漏洞的工作原理：攻击者通过恶意构造Chart.yaml文件和符号链接（symlink）指向敏感文件，当执行`helm dependency update`时，Helm会跟随符号链接，将恶意代码写入目标文件，导致代码执行。该观点强调了Helm未验证目标文件的问题。
• [ivan4th] 对Helm整体设计提出批评，尤其是使用文本模板引擎生成YAML的机制，认为这是问题的根源。该评论更像是一种对Helm使用体验的抱怨，而非直接针对漏洞本身。
• [codebastard] 质疑攻击的实际可行性，指出攻击者需要文件系统访问权限和Helm仓库的访问权限。如果攻击者已经具备这些权限，是否还存在更大的安全隐患？该观点认为漏洞的危险性被夸大。
• [TheDong] 对漏洞描述的清晰度提出质疑，特别是关于`Chart.lock`如何成为符号链接以及为何修复只针对`Chart.lock`。该评论建议修复方案应为禁止图表包含指向根目录之外的符号链接。
• [Sjoerd] 关注攻击场景和安全边界问题，询问攻击者如何将恶意仓库传递给受害者以及Helm通常是否以特权用户身份运行。该观点认为漏洞描述缺乏对这些关键问题的解答。
• [mkagenius] 提到类似工具（如aider、claude desktop）要求shell访问权限的风险，认为允许LLM通过shell执行生成图表是一个不好的做法。
• [xyst] 认为该漏洞很有趣，并提到自己通过Nix管理配置文件，从而能够检测到恶意写入尝试。建议使用只读分区和“诱饵”文件来防御此类攻击。
• [quotemstr] 讽刺地提到内存安全语言中不应出现安全漏洞，暗示对漏洞存在的惊讶。
• [sugarpimpdorsey] 批评YAML格式本身，认为其设计有问题，并预测这不会是YAML相关的最后一个远程代码执行（RCE）漏洞。
• [qxfys] 好奇此类漏洞是否可以通过LLM自动发现，询问其他人的经验。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于漏洞的实际危险性和攻击的可行性。部分评论认为攻击者需要过多的权限，漏洞的威胁被夸大，而其他人则关注漏洞的根本原因和修复方案。
• 对YAML格式本身的批评以及对Helm设计的不满也是讨论中的一个分支，显示出部分用户对现有工具链的深层次不满。
• 最后，关于LLM是否能够自动发现此类漏洞的讨论，表明了对人工智能技术在安全领域应用的潜在兴趣和探索。

Patched versions

Description
A Helm contributor discovered that a specially crafted
Chart.yaml
file along with a specially linked
Chart.lock
file can lead to local code execution when dependencies are updated.
Impact
Fields in a
Chart.yaml
file, that are carried over to a
Chart.lock
file when dependencies are updated and this file is written, can be crafted in a way that can cause execution if that same content were in a file that is executed (e.g., a
bash.rc
file or shell script). If the
Chart.lock
file is symlinked to one of these files updating dependencies will write the lock file content to the symlinked file. This can lead to unwanted execution. Helm warns of the symlinked file but did not stop execution due to symlinking.
This affects when dependencies are updated. When using the
helm
command this happens when
helm dependency update
is run.
helm dependency build
can write a lock file when one does not exist but this vector requires one to already exist. This affects the Helm SDK when the downloader
Manager
performs an update.

This issue has been resolved in Helm v3.18.4
Workarounds
Ensure the
Chart.lock
file in a chart is not a symlink prior to updating dependencies.

document.

44506696.article_summary: 文章主要介绍了Helm中的一个高危安全漏洞（CVE-2025-53547）。在Helm版本≤3.18.3中，恶意构造的`Chart.yaml`文件和符号链接的`Chart.lock`文件可能导致本地代码执行。当用户运行`helm dependency update`时，某些字段会被带入`Chart.lock`文件，如果该文件被符号链接到可执行文件（如`bash.rc`或shell脚本），可能导致 unwanted 的代码执行。此问题已在Helm v3.18.4中修复。作为临时解决方案，用户应确保`Chart.lock`文件不是符号链接。漏洞的CVSS评分为8.5，属于高危级别。
44506696.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Helm图表依赖更新过程中存在的安全漏洞及其潜在的攻击向量和影响

不同观点：
• [yelirekim] 详细解释了漏洞的工作原理：攻击者通过恶意构造Chart.yaml文件和符号链接（symlink）指向敏感文件，当执行`helm dependency update`时，Helm会跟随符号链接，将恶意代码写入目标文件，导致代码执行。该观点强调了Helm未验证目标文件的问题。
• [ivan4th] 对Helm整体设计提出批评，尤其是使用文本模板引擎生成YAML的机制，认为这是问题的根源。该评论更像是一种对Helm使用体验的抱怨，而非直接针对漏洞本身。
• [codebastard] 质疑攻击的实际可行性，指出攻击者需要文件系统访问权限和Helm仓库的访问权限。如果攻击者已经具备这些权限，是否还存在更大的安全隐患？该观点认为漏洞的危险性被夸大。
• [TheDong] 对漏洞描述的清晰度提出质疑，特别是关于`Chart.lock`如何成为符号链接以及为何修复只针对`Chart.lock`。该评论建议修复方案应为禁止图表包含指向根目录之外的符号链接。
• [Sjoerd] 关注攻击场景和安全边界问题，询问攻击者如何将恶意仓库传递给受害者以及Helm通常是否以特权用户身份运行。该观点认为漏洞描述缺乏对这些关键问题的解答。
• [mkagenius] 提到类似工具（如aider、claude desktop）要求shell访问权限的风险，认为允许LLM通过shell执行生成图表是一个不好的做法。
• [xyst] 认为该漏洞很有趣，并提到自己通过Nix管理配置文件，从而能够检测到恶意写入尝试。建议使用只读分区和“诱饵”文件来防御此类攻击。
• [quotemstr] 讽刺地提到内存安全语言中不应出现安全漏洞，暗示对漏洞存在的惊讶。
• [sugarpimpdorsey] 批评YAML格式本身，认为其设计有问题，并预测这不会是YAML相关的最后一个远程代码执行（RCE）漏洞。
• [qxfys] 好奇此类漏洞是否可以通过LLM自动发现，询问其他人的经验。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于漏洞的实际危险性和攻击的可行性。部分评论认为攻击者需要过多的权限，漏洞的威胁被夸大，而其他人则关注漏洞的根本原因和修复方案。
• 对YAML格式本身的批评以及对Helm设计的不满也是讨论中的一个分支，显示出部分用户对现有工具链的深层次不满。
• 最后，关于LLM是否能够自动发现此类漏洞的讨论，表明了对人工智能技术在安全领域应用的潜在兴趣和探索。

data.title: Most RESTful APIs aren't really RESTful
data.author: BerislavLopac
data.article_summary: Roy T. Fielding的论文《架构风格与基于网络的软件架构设计》介绍了REST（表现层状态转移）架构风格，旨在分析不同架构风格的优缺点，强调REST在可扩展性、简洁性和适应性方面的优势。REST为设计分布式系统提供了原则和约束，特别是通过使用无状态接口和基于资源的交互。Fielding批评了许多自称“RESTful”的API，因为它们未能实现REST的核心约束，尤其是缺乏超媒体作为应用状态引擎（HATEOAS）。HATEOAS要求客户端通过服务器响应中的超媒体链接动态发现可执行操作，从而减少客户端与服务器之间的耦合。关于“资源”，Fielding指出，任何可命名的信息都可以是资源，其关键在于资源标识符的分配和表示的关联，而非服务器上的具体实体。因此，实现HATEOAS比争论API中是否允许使用动词更符合REST原则。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：REST和HATEOAS的实际应用及其与现代API设计的契合度

不同观点：
• cjpearson认为，"REST API"这个术语已经经历了语义扩散，实际使用中通常指的是返回JSON数据、CRUD操作映射到HTTP动词、状态码争论等特征。他认为可以接受这种普遍理解，而不是严格遵循Fielding论文中的定义。
• mixedbit指出，经过多年实践，发现真正的REST（特别是自发现API）在大多数情况下并不实际。他强调Fielding的论文没有提供完整的实施细节，且实现自发现API需要额外的努力，但收益有限。他还认为REST的目标与良好的用户体验不兼容。
• salmonellaeater认为，REST API设计适用于用户通过代理（如浏览器）与API交互的场景，而非特定应用程序的展示控制。他建议只有在真正符合REST设计的情况下才应称之为REST。
• BrenBarn强调，严格的REST原则在常见情况下并不具备良好的成本效益比。他以微波炉为例，说明按部就班的操作可能比动态发现更简单直接。
• recursivedoubts补充，使用RESTful/HATEOAS模式需要符合的客户端，这增加了实施的复杂性。
• _heimdall指出，REST和HATEOAS在API消费者是第三方的情况下更有益，而对于前端应用专门针对后端的场景，其收益往往不抵成本。
• nirui认为，编程世界中很多标准在实际应用中会被修改和调整，以适应实际需求和生产力。
• Scarblac提到，UI设计师希望对页面外观有详细控制，而完全依赖API响应进行动态渲染的客户端无法实现这种控制。
• dwaltrip质疑HATEOAS的实用性，询问是否有实际使用场景，并怀疑自动发现客户端的可行性。
• sublinear指出，通过HATEOAS和模式定义可以实现动态导航，但实际应用中可能导致不必要的复杂性和耦合问题。
• mschaef认为，HATEOAS解决的客户端-服务器耦合问题并没有真正消失，只是转移到了文档结构中，且JSON缺乏XML的丰富类型结构，使得纯REST/HATEOAS更难实现。
• bazoom42建议将REST API称为HTTP API，因为REST最初是为人类导航的信息系统设计的，而非程序API。
• alkonaut将REST的定义演变与面向对象编程语言的演变相比较，认为术语的含义会随着广泛使用而改变。
• thom认为，严格遵循REST原则并不能显著改善API，实际项目中更重视功能的实现。
• dewey总结，学术上的正确性在实际功能开发中往往不如实际需求重要。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于REST和HATEOAS的实际应用价值，特别是在现代API设计中是否必要和可行。
• 讨论还涉及术语的演变和实际使用中的妥协，以及不同开发者对REST原则的不同理解和接受程度。

44507076.article_content:
When talking about REST, it is worth reading
the dissertation
of Roy Thomas Fielding. The
original paper
that describes RESTful web, “Architectural Styles and the Design of Network-based Software Architectures” Roy T. Fielding (2000), introduces the Representational State Transfer (REST) architectural style as a framework for designing scalable, performant, and maintainable networked systems, particularly web services.
The paper aims to analyze architectural styles for network-based systems, identifying their strengths and weaknesses. It defines REST as a specific architectural style optimized for the modern web, focusing on scalability, simplicity, and adaptability.
Fielding demonstrates how REST principles shape the success of the web, advocating for its adoption in designing distributed systems with universal, stateless interfaces and clear resource-based interactions.
In his dissertation he does
not
prescribe the specific use of HTTP verbs (like GET, POST, PUT, DELETE) or focus on CRUD-style APIs as REST is often implemented today.
The dissertation clearly describes REST as an architectural style that provides principles and constraints for building network-based applications, using the web as its foundational example.
Roy Fielding has explicitly criticized the oversimplification of REST in CRUD-style APIs, emphasizing that many so-called “RESTful” APIs fail to implement key REST constraints, particularly the use of hypermedia for driving application state transitions. In his 2008 blog post, “REST APIs must be hypertext-driven,” Fielding states:
“If the engine of application state (and hence the API) is not being driven by hypertext, then it cannot be RESTful and cannot be a REST API. Period.”
Source
This underscores his view that without hypermedia controls, an API does not fulfill the REST architectural style Hypermedia controls are elements embedded in a resource representation that guide clients on what actions they can take next.
Common misconceptions in the context of what people consider REST are for example:
REST is CRUD (often it is, but not always)
A resource is an entity (often meaning a persistence entity).
RESTful API must not use verbs.
But those are actually
design decision
made for the API at hand, chosen by their creators and have nothing to do with REST.
What Does “Driven by Hypertext” Mean?
The phrase “not being driven by hypertext” in Roy Fielding’s criticism refers to the absence of Hypermedia as the Engine of Application State (
HATEOAS
) in many APIs that claim to be RESTful. HATEOAS is a fundamental principle of REST, requiring that the client dynamically discover actions and interactions through hypermedia links embedded in server responses, rather than relying on out-of-band knowledge (e.g., API documentation).
{
"orderId"

123
,
"_links"
:
{
"self"

{
"href"

"/orders/123"
},

{
"href"

"/orders/123/cancel"
,
"method"
:
"POST"
}
}
}
The core problem it addresses is client-server coupling. There are probably countless projects where a small change in a server’s URI structure required a coordinated (and often painful) deployment of multiple client applications. A HATEOAS-driven approach directly solves this by decoupling the client from the server’s namespace. This addresses the quality of evolvability.
Simply implementing HATEOAS will bring you closer to RESTful principles than debating whether verbs are allowed in your API.
What is a “Resource”?
Often people argue about what a resource in REST is. I’ve seen more or less commonly people expressing the opinion that a resource is a data structure coming from the server, unfortunately often even equal to a persistence entity.
Let’s check what Fielding says about it:
The key abstraction of information in REST is a resource.
Any information that can be named can be a resource: a document or image, a temporal service (e.g. “today’s weather in Los Angeles”), a collection of other resources, a non-virtual object (e.g. a person), and so on. In other words, any concept that might be the target of an author’s hypertext reference must fit within the definition of a resource. A resource is a conceptual mapping to a set of entities, not the entity that corresponds to the mapping at any particular point in time.
Semantics are a by-product of the act of assigning resource identifiers and populating those resources with representations. At no time whatsoever do the server or client software need to know or understand the meaning of a URI – they merely act as a conduit through which the creator of a resource (a human naming authority) can associate representations with the semantics identified by the URI. In other words, there are no resources on the server; just mechanisms that supply answers across an abstract interface defined by resources. It may seem odd, but this is the essence of what makes the Web work across so many different implementations.
Now let’s take a look at
RFC 3986

data.title: People having phone sex on FaceTime will now get a warning from Apple
data.author: chrisjj
data.article_summary: 苹果即将发布的iOS 26软件更新中，FaceTime可能加入一项安全功能：当检测到裸体时，视频会自动暂停，并提示用户是否继续通话或结束通话。该功能利用设备上的机器学习技术，在本地分析图像，不会将数据传输至苹果服务器。尽管默认设置为关闭，用户可以自行选择开启或关闭此敏感内容警告。此举旨在保护年轻用户，但也引发了对隐私和通话体验的讨论。苹果尚未对此功能发表评论。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：苹果FaceTime敏感内容警告功能的技术实现和隐私影响

不同观点：
• **[kylecazar]的观点：**
  - FaceTime设置中有一个选项可以打开或关闭敏感内容警告，且默认是关闭的。这表明该功能可能不会自动应用到所有用户的手机上，或者至少用户可以选择关闭该功能。
  - 图像分析是在手机本地进行的，不会将任何数据传输到苹果的服务器，从而保护用户隐私。

• **[thatgerhard]的观点：**
  - 对苹果如何识别敏感内容表示疑问，质疑如果没有数据传输到苹果服务器，苹果如何能判断内容是否为敏感内容。

补充讨论：
- **隐私与功能的平衡**：[kylecazar]提到图像在本地分析，强调了用户隐私的保护，但[thatgerhard]的质疑反映了用户对苹果如何实现这一功能的透明度的关注。
- **用户选择权**：[kylecazar]指出用户可以选择关闭该功能，这体现了对用户自主权的重视。
- **争议焦点**：苹果如何在不传输数据到服务器的情况下准确识别敏感内容，这是用户对该功能技术实现的主要疑问和争议点。

44518978.article_content:
Mood about to be ruined by the video being frozen? (Picture: Getty)
The lighting is low, the expectation high, and your partner starts unbuttoning their shirt.
Suddenly, you see the FaceTime video freeze, and a black message fills the screen.
‘Audio and video are paused because you may be showing something sensitive,’ your
phone
informs you.
‘If you feel uncomfortable, you should end the call.’
Kind of a buzz kill? This could be what awaits iPhone users in the next software update, which is reported to include it as a security feature.
The feature was first spotted by iDeviceHelp, who wrote on X: ‘In iOS 26 FaceTime will pause the Video if you’re undressing while on a FaceTime call here’s the on screen prompt warning that you get asking if you would like to resume audio and video or End the call’.
The screen shown to users if nudity is detected
It’s not clear if this is a glitch, intended only for accounts used by children, or if it is intended to be rolled out to everyone.
The developer beta version is reportedly showing this to any users who strip off, even those well into middle age.
If you go to the settings for FaceTime, there is an option to toggle Sensitive Content Warning on or off.
It is off by default, indicating that it may not actually come to everyone’s phones, or at least that you’ll have an option to turn it off.
Apple has not yet commented on it.
Does this mean Apple is spying on my sexy phone calls?
Not quite. Images are analysed locally on the phone, with nothing transmitted to Apple’s servers.
According to the company, ‘Communication Safety uses on-device machine learning to analyze photo and video attachments and determine if a photo or video appears to contain nudity.
‘Because the photos and videos are analysed on your child’s device, Apple doesn’t receive an indication that nudity was detected and doesn’t get access to the photos or videos as a result.’

44518978.article_summary: 苹果即将发布的iOS 26软件更新中，FaceTime可能加入一项安全功能：当检测到裸体时，视频会自动暂停，并提示用户是否继续通话或结束通话。该功能利用设备上的机器学习技术，在本地分析图像，不会将数据传输至苹果服务器。尽管默认设置为关闭，用户可以自行选择开启或关闭此敏感内容警告。此举旨在保护年轻用户，但也引发了对隐私和通话体验的讨论。苹果尚未对此功能发表评论。
44518978.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：苹果FaceTime敏感内容警告功能的技术实现和隐私影响

不同观点：
• **[kylecazar]的观点：**
  - FaceTime设置中有一个选项可以打开或关闭敏感内容警告，且默认是关闭的。这表明该功能可能不会自动应用到所有用户的手机上，或者至少用户可以选择关闭该功能。
  - 图像分析是在手机本地进行的，不会将任何数据传输到苹果的服务器，从而保护用户隐私。

• **[thatgerhard]的观点：**
  - 对苹果如何识别敏感内容表示疑问，质疑如果没有数据传输到苹果服务器，苹果如何能判断内容是否为敏感内容。

补充讨论：
- **隐私与功能的平衡**：[kylecazar]提到图像在本地分析，强调了用户隐私的保护，但[thatgerhard]的质疑反映了用户对苹果如何实现这一功能的透明度的关注。
- **用户选择权**：[kylecazar]指出用户可以选择关闭该功能，这体现了对用户自主权的重视。
- **争议焦点**：苹果如何在不传输数据到服务器的情况下准确识别敏感内容，这是用户对该功能技术实现的主要疑问和争议点。

主要讨论点：AI工具对电影/视频创作的影响及未来发展

不同观点：
• consumer451认为AI工具降低了电影和视频制作的门槛，使得更多人可以创作出高质量的内容。他强调，这个项目并非由AI“神奇地创造”，而是被AI所赋能。他还提供了一个链接，列出了用于该项目的具体工具，表明AI只是辅助创作的一部分。

• reify持更激进的观点，认为AI的发展将导致好莱坞及整个电影/电视产业的消亡。他认为，在不久的将来，个体将拥有足够的创意能力来创作任何他们想要的内容，市场上将会充斥大量创意和风险承担的内容，最优秀的内容将脱颖而出。他还质疑大型电影公司能否适应这种变化并生存下来。

补充讨论：
• consumer451对AI工具持积极态度，认为它们扩展了创作的可能性，并强调工具的作用而非完全取代人类创作。
• reify的观点更为悲观，预测传统电影制作行业的消亡，并强调个体创作能力的提升将带来市场变化。
• reify的评论还带有对AI写作的讽刺（"written by an ai Muppet!"），显示出对AI生成内容的某种不信任或不屑。

争议焦点：
• AI工具是赋能创作还是取代人类创作。
• 电影和电视行业是否会因AI技术的发展而消亡。
• AI生成内容的质量和市场影响。

data.title: Astro is a return to the fundamentals of the web
data.author: pumbaa
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕Astro框架及其相关技术（如JavaScript岛屿架构、静态页面生成、传统与现代前端框架对比）的讨论。

不同观点：
• **Astro的优点和使用体验**：
  - **[diggan]** 和 **[thibaultamartin]** 支持Astro，认为它通过JavaScript岛屿架构实现了类似"渐进增强"的传统网页开发方式，页面默认是静态HTML，只在需要交互的部分引入JavaScript。Astro优化了速度，并且开发体验简单愉快。
  - **[rasmus1610]** 分享了实际项目中的正面体验，使用Astro构建的网站比WordPress更易维护，且可以免费托管在Netlify等平台上。
  - **[evklein]** 也表示Astro的开发体验非常好，特别是可以控制JavaScript的使用量。

• **对Astro及其架构的质疑**：
  - **[poushkar]** 指出"传统框架"通常指SPA和虚拟DOM框架，但实际上像Backbone和jQuery等更早的框架已经采用类似的开发方式。
  - **[kh_hk]** 认为Astro的岛屿架构在某些情况下不一定有效，如果只是为了生成静态HTML，可能根本不需要那么多JavaScript。
  - **[sublinear]** 质疑Astro相对于纯静态页面的优势，认为如果不依赖框架可能会更好。

• **与其他框架的比较**：
  - **[teekoiv]** 认为Astro和NextJS在静态页面生成方面不如SvelteKit灵活，尤其是处理动态路径时。
  - **[exiguus]** 提到Astro的岛屿架构允许实现微前端，这对于多团队协作的大型项目可能有益，但这种架构也有其缺点。
  - **[ttoinou]** 对Astro和Deno+Fresh框架的区别感到困惑，认为两者在架构上相似，但缺乏性能对比数据。

• **对前端开发状态的批判**：
  - **[aswerty]** 认为前端开发领域的讨论已经变得混乱，框架之间的比较往往流于表面，如"速度更快"或"体验更好"等模糊论点，缺乏实质性分析。
  - **[pjmlp]** 指出Web开发的基本原理没有改变，但JavaScript框架的流行让开发变得复杂，建议回归基础。

• **对CMS功能的关注**：
  - **[pentagrama]** 关心Astro是否具备类似WordPress的CMS功能，特别是对普通用户是否友好。

• **对Web开发工具链的批评**：
  - **[wackget]** 认为现代Web开发中的构建步骤和包管理工具并不属于Web的基本原理，质疑这些工具的必要性。

• **对Next.js的反对意见**：
  - **[Zealotux]** 不建议将Next.js作为React框架的默认选择，推荐Remix和TanStack等替代方案。

补充讨论：
- 讨论中多次提到Astro的"岛屿架构"及其在大型项目中的优势，但也有人质疑这种架构的必要性和实际效果。
- 对前端开发工具和框架的流行趋势存在批判性思考，特别是对JavaScript框架的复杂性和必要性提出质疑。
- 提到了Astro与WordPress等传统CMS系统的对比，以及用户对CMS功能的需求。

data.title: GlobalFoundries to Acquire MIPS
data.author: mshockwave
data.article_summary: 2025年7月8日，全球知名半导体制造商GlobalFoundries（GF）宣布收购AI和处理器IP供应商MIPS，以增强其在人工智能和计算能力方面的产品组合。此次收购将为GF带来基于RISC-V架构的先进处理器IP和软件工具，适用于自动驾驶、工业自动化、数据中心和智能边缘计算等领域。MIPS近期推出了Atlas产品组合及虚拟平台Atlas Explorer，旨在优化性能、功耗和设计周期。收购完成后，MIPS将作为GF的独立业务运营，继续服务于广泛技术领域的客户。此次收购预计在2025年下半年完成。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：MIPS和RISC-V架构的发展及市场竞争

不同观点：
• somanyphotons认为，拥有旧晶圆厂和内部CPU设计团队的公司可能通过亏损销售来获取低端市场的份额。这暗示了市场竞争策略和公司财务状况的问题。
• sloemoe关注架构技术细节，提到延迟槽（delay slot）的概念，并指出许多架构仍在使用它，暗示了对技术历史和现状的兴趣。
• musicale对比MIPS和RISC-V，认为MIPS错失了开放架构的机会，否则RISC-V可能不会出现。他强调了MIPS的早期优势和潜在的市场错失。
• somanyphotons还提出了关于RISC-V的CPU IP供应商的财务状况问题，并询问是否正在出现市场整合的迹象。
• stevefan1999用调侃的方式提到AMD和MIPS之间的关系，暗示了行业内的公司动态和历史变迁。
• alephnerd对MIPS和RISC-V的结合表示关注，认为这是芯片设计和制造领域的一种互补尝试，特别是对于嵌入式用例。他还提到RISC-V在人才和资本上的聚集效应。

补充讨论：
• 评论中涉及到的技术细节（如延迟槽）表明了对不同架构技术特点的关注。
• 讨论中多次提到市场竞争和策略，包括亏损销售以获取市场份额和市场整合的可能性。
• 评论也涉及了行业历史和公司动态，如AMD和MIPS之间的关系变化，这为讨论增加了一个行业发展的维度。
• 对RISC-V和MIPS未来发展的看法，特别是RISC-V在人才和资本上的聚集，预示着对未来技术趋势的展望。

44501821.article_content:
Discover the Latest from MIPS
Product News, Industry Insights, Announcements, and More
GlobalFoundries to Acquire MIPS to Accelerate AI and Compute Capabilities
July 8, 2025
Acquisition will expand GF portfolio with cutting-edge RISC-V processor IP and software tools for real-time computing in autonomous mobility, industrial automation, datacenter and intelligent edge applications
MALTA, N.Y., and San Jose, Calif., July 8, 2025
– GlobalFoundries (Nasdaq: GFS) (GF) today announced a definitive agreement to acquire MIPS, a leading supplier of AI and processor IP. This strategic acquisition will expand GF’s portfolio of customizable IP offerings, allowing it to further differentiate its process technologies with IP and software capabilities.
“MIPS brings a strong heritage of delivering efficient, scalable compute IP tailored for performance-critical applications, which strategically aligns with the evolving demands of AI platforms across diverse markets,” said Niels Anderskouv, president and chief operating officer at GlobalFoundries. “Through this acquisition, we will expand our capabilities to offer customers more flexible, RISC-V-based open platform solutions, paired with our differentiated process technologies and world-class manufacturing to help them build world-class products. This acquisition will be a powerful step forward to push the boundaries of efficiency and performance across a broad range of applications in automotive, industrial and datacenter infrastructure.”
MIPS recently expanded its processor IP offerings, based on open RISC-V specification, with the launch of its Atlas portfolio, a comprehensive suite of compute cores designed for real-time and application processing as well as specialized AI edge processing cores. Additionally, MIPS also introduced Atlas Explorer, a virtual platform that enables optimization of performance, power and area to shift-left in the design cycle.
“Becoming part of GlobalFoundries marks the start of a bold new chapter for MIPS,” said Sameer Wasson, CEO of MIPS. “GF’s proven track record in delivering differentiated technologies through a secure, global manufacturing footprint will enhance our ability to accelerate innovation and scale our solutions—unlocking new opportunities in the Physical AI space and driving even greater value for our customers.”
The acquisition of MIPS is subject to the satisfaction of customary closing conditions, including the receipt of required regulatory approvals, and is expected to be completed in the second half of 2025. Following the acquisition, MIPS will continue to operate as a standalone business within GF and serve its customers across a broad range of technologies.
About MIPS
MIPS is the leading provider of compute subsystems for autonomous platforms in automotive, industrial, and embedded markets. With a 40-year heritage in RISC computing innovation and safety capable processing, MIPS is uniquely positioned to simplify the adoption of Physical AI in industrial robotics and automotive applications. MIPS technology is based on the open specification RISC-V instruction set architecture, featuring MIPS pioneering, patented, multi-threaded capabilities to move beyond proprietary legacy architecture lock-ins. For more information, please visit MIPS.com.
About GF
GlobalFoundries (GF) is a leading manufacturer of essential semiconductors the world relies on to live, work and connect. We innovate and partner with customers to deliver more power-efficient, high-performance products for the automotive, smart mobile devices, internet of things, communications infrastructure and other high-growth markets. With our global manufacturing footprint spanning the U.S., Europe and Asia, GF is a trusted and reliable source for customers around the world. Every day, our talented and diverse team delivers results with an unyielding focus on security, longevity and sustainability. For more information, visit www.gf.com.

data.title: Swahili on the Road
data.author: Thevet
data.article_summary: 本文探讨斯瓦希里语如何成为东非的通用语言。作者提到，1960年，坦桑尼亚民族主义领袖尼雷尔在电视节目中为非洲独立辩护，强调殖民地人民有权收回自己的“外套”，即独立权。虽然尼雷尔在国际场合使用英语，但在国内他积极推广斯瓦希里语。斯瓦希里语成为东非的通用语言并非偶然，而是经过历史和政治进程的推动，特别是在去殖民化背景下，尼雷尔等领导人的倡导起到了关键作用。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：斯瓦西里语的历史根源及其在东非的重要性

不同观点：
• pazimzadeh引用了《自然》杂志的一篇文章，强调中世纪斯瓦西里海岸居民具有非洲和波斯混合血统的证据，尤其是在公元1000年左右。这种混合与考古学证据和斯瓦西里海岸的文化转型（如伊斯兰教的广泛传播）相吻合。他还提到波斯词汇对斯瓦西里语的贡献，但具体来源尚不清楚。

• georgeg从东非人的角度出发，认为文章未能充分解释斯瓦西里语在东非的重要性和历史背景。他指出，坦桑尼亚在殖民后才采用斯瓦西里语，而该语言在东非沿海（从索马里到莫桑比克）作为贸易语言已有千年历史。他还强调斯瓦西里语是班图语、阿拉伯语及一些葡萄牙语词汇的融合体，并且在东非、中非和南非的班图地区易于理解和使用。他认为将斯瓦西里语的成功归因于坦桑尼亚是短视的。

补充讨论：
• callistus对pazimzadeh分享的文章表示感谢，并特别提到尼雷尔（坦桑尼亚首任总统）对斯瓦西里语推广的贡献。

• muragekibicho提到在肯尼亚内罗毕无法访问文章链接，可能是因为网站问题或地域限制。

争议焦点：
• 斯瓦西里语的历史重要性及其在东非广泛使用的原因。georgeg认为文章忽视了斯瓦西里语在贸易和跨文化交流中的历史角色，并将坦桑尼亚作为语言成功的核心原因是一种短视的观点。

44505359.article_content:
Behind the Times
Swahili on the Road
How did Swahili become an East African lingua franca? It was not by accident.
Morgan J. Robinson
| Published in
History Today
Volume 75 Issue 7 July 2025
I
n March 1960 Julius Nyerere – then leader of the Tanganyika African National Union (TANU) – sat down with former first lady Eleanor Roosevelt on her roundtable discussion programme
Prospects of Mankind
. The topic was ‘Africa: A Revolution in Haste’. Although he found himself in a sympathetic circle of interlocutors, Nyerere was asked to defend the ‘readiness’ of African peoples for independence. Good-humoured but resolute, he replied: ‘If you come into my house and steal my jacket, don’t then ask me whether I am ready for my jacket. The jacket was mine, you had no right at all to take it from me … I may not look as smart in it as you look in it, but it’s mine.’ With a simple analogy, Nyerere swept aside the argument that decolonisation was happening too quickly. And though this defence was delivered in composed and commanding English – the language of his degrees at Makerere College in Uganda and Edinburgh University – the language that Nyerere championed at home was Swahili.

data.title: Mini robots detect and fix water pipe leaks without digging
data.author: Bluestein
data.article_summary: 文章介绍了英国谢菲尔德大学研发的**Pipebots**机器人，它们可以进入地下水管检测和修复漏水问题，避免传统维修需要挖开道路的做法。这些机器人配备声学传感器、摄像头和坚固的轮子，能够穿越狭窄、弯曲的管道，并将问题细节传回地面工程师。Pipebots是英国现代化老旧水基础设施计划的一部分，目标是提高维护效率、降低成本，并防止漏水污染。这类机器人有望在全球范围内，尤其是发展中国家，帮助更有效地管理水资源。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：管道机器人技术的可行性、创新性及其在实际应用中的挑战

不同观点：
• **技术需求与市场验证**：mike_hearn质疑该技术是否已与水务公司验证过需求，指出像Thames Water等公司已经采用高科技手段如地下麦克风和化学试剂来检测泄漏，并怀疑该技术是否有市场优势。
• **实际应用环境**：evrimoztamur担心机器人在污浊环境中会被堵塞，如遭遇“fatberg”（油脂堵塞），质疑其在实际复杂环境中的应用效果。
• **电流检测法**：presidentender提到一种通过电流检测管道破裂的方法，并指出该方法在PVC管道中的应用限制，同时分享了一个因方法简单而难以商业化的案例。
• **网站设计问题**：mlok抱怨某网站设计不佳，导致其快速退出，属于用户体验方面的反馈。
• **类似技术对比**：zubiaur指出在石油和天然气行业已有“智能猪”用于检测管道问题，认为这些机器人如果应用在低风险场合是可以接受的。
• **历史对比**：prewett提到古代美索不达米亚的水下修复方法，将其与现代技术对比，提供了历史视角。
• **现有技术实例**：josephkaz提到CISBOT，一种用于封堵铸铁燃气管道泄漏的机器人，指出该技术已经在伦敦和纽约应用。
• **机械设计讨论**：mattlondon对机器人无轮但有辐条腿的设计提出疑问，认为可能是为了越过管道间的障碍，并分享了自己的实际需求。

补充讨论：
• **其他类似技术公司**：mvf4z7提到美国另一家开发类似技术的公司MotMot.ai，扩展了讨论范围。
• **文化联想**：libraryatnight联想到《星际迷航》中的纳米机器人情节，表达了对机器人技术发展的期待，同时对AI取代人类工作的趋势表示担忧。

争议焦点：
• **技术创新性与市场需求之间的矛盾**：mike_hearn质疑该技术是否有市场优势，而zubiaur和josephkaz则认为该技术是现有方法的自然延伸或补充。
• **实际应用中的技术挑战**：evrimoztamur和mattlondon分别对机器人在污浊环境中的表现和机械设计的实用性提出了实际应用中的挑战。

总结：讨论围绕管道机器人技术的市场需求、实际应用效果、机械设计及历史背景展开，涉及现有技术的比较和用户体验反馈，体现了对该技术创新性和实用性的多角度审视。

Fixing underground water pipes usually means digging up roads and sidewalks — a process that's disruptive and expensive. However, researchers at the University of Sheffield in the U.K. are working on a different approach. They've developed small robots called "Pipebots" that can travel inside water pipes to find and potentially repair leaks, all without any excavation.

Get my best tech tips, urgent security alerts, and exclusive deals delivered straight to your inbox. Plus, you’ll get instant access to my Ultimate Scam Survival Guide — free when you join my

Pipebot in various environments.
(University of Sheffield)
Old leaky underground pipes are causing a crisis
The U.K. has some of the oldest water systems in the world, with parts of the network still dating back to the Victorian era. Not surprisingly, many of these pipes are leaking, wasting about 790 million gallons of water every day. Fixing them usually means digging up streets, which causes major disruption and adds to the country's $5 billion a year maintenance costs.
A prototype of a Pipebot.
(University of Sheffield)
Little robots come to the rescue
Pipebots are tiny, high-tech helpers designed to navigate the underground world of water pipes. Each one comes with acoustic sensors, cameras, and rugged wheels that help it move through tight, twisty spaces-while smart enough to steer clear of off-limits areas.
They're dropped into the water system through hydrants and travel in groups, scanning the inside of pipes for even the smallest cracks. When they spot a problem, they send the details back to engineers above ground, making it easier to fix issues without digging anything up.
An illustration showing that a Pipebot has found a leak.
(University of Sheffield)
The robots are part of a bigger innovation plan
These robots are part of a larger effort to modernize how the U.K. manages its aging water infrastructure. The initiative isn't just a university research project-it's supported by the U.K.'s water regulator, OFWAT (the Water Services Regulation Authority), and involves several collaborative projects.
One of these projects focuses on using Pipebots to inspect live, pressurized wastewater pipes, also known as raising mains. The goal is to catch problems early and make repairs before leaks cause pollution.
Another project, called "no dig leak repair," is working on ways to fix leaks from inside the water mains themselves, completely avoiding the need for disruptive roadwork.
There's also the EU-funded Pipeon Project, which is developing advanced, AI-powered robots that can inspect sewers autonomously, without human guidance.
Image of a Pipebot.
(University of Sheffield)
Kurt's key takeaways
These little robots could be exactly what countries everywhere need to keep their water systems running smoothly. They have the potential to make maintenance cleaner, more affordable, and way more efficient. That's especially important for developing countries where budgets are tight and infrastructure is aging or incomplete. As the pressure to conserve water grows, tools like Pipebots could make a real difference in helping us manage this vital resource more wisely.

data.title: Is Gemini 2.5 good at bounding boxes?
data.author: simedw
data.article_summary: 文章主要评估了Gemini 2.5 Pro在对象检测任务中的表现，特别是在MS-COCO数据集上的 bounding box 检测能力。结果显示，Gemini 2.5 Pro 的表现与2018年的Yolo V3模型相当。作者通过多种设置（包括有无结构化输出和不同token预算）进行了测试，发现Pro版本优于Flash和Flash-Lite版本，且不使用思考预算时表现更好。整体来看，Gemini 2.5在对象检测上表现尚可，但并未超越传统的CNN模型。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：多模态大语言模型（VLM）在目标检测任务中的表现及相关技术细节，包括其与专门计算机视觉工具的比较、性能差异以及应用场景。

不同观点：
• thegeomaster认为，Google的Gemini模型在边界框检测任务中表现出色，尤其是经过后训练（post-training）后，基础的多模态LLM如果没有这种后训练，性能会差很多。
• fzysingularity指出，大多数VLM在定位任务上表现不佳，即使经过目标检测任务的后训练。不同模型的坐标系不一致，如Gemini和Qwen使用的坐标格式不同，这给新用户带来了困扰。他们选择将目标检测任务交给专门工具，因为像Gemini这样的模型在性能上（mAP 0.34）不如DETR等架构（mAP 0.6）。
• smus的实验表明，Gemini 2.5在零样本（zero-shot）情况下表现良好，但在提供视觉和文本示例后性能下降，说明其在结合额外上下文信息方面存在不足。
• serjester分享了Gemini在PDF边界框任务中的成功应用，认为其在精确检测方面表现突出。
• sly010对LLM如何进行目标检测感到困惑，质疑为何Gemini 2和2.5的视觉能力不同，并期望所有模型都能访问相同的最先进视觉模型。
• chrismorgan质疑所谓“地面真值”（ground truth）的准确性，认为MS-COCO数据集并不完全可靠。
• bee_rider关注功率消耗和注释工作，建议使用Gemini作为注释工具，以节省时间和精力。
• xrendan指出，Gemini在处理未训练过的任务（如PCB原理图）时表现不佳。
• mkagenius分享了他们在Android工具开发中的经验，发现Gemini在规划和查找任务中表现出色，优于其他模型。
• mehulashah在文档分割任务中比较了Gemini与其他现代OCR模型，发现DETR架构模型在性能上更优。
• muxamilian认为Gemini的输出在很多情况下优于COCO的地面真值数据。

• nolok分享了个人使用Gemini的体验，发现其在复杂任务中表现出色，但在简单任务中有时会出错。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中多次提到不同模型的坐标系不一致问题，这给实际应用带来了困扰。
• 有对LLM如何进行非文本任务（如目标检测）的机制探讨，以及对模型性能差异的疑惑。
• 对地面真值数据集的可靠性提出质疑，强调了实验和比较的重要性。
• 提出了结合传统计算机视觉技术和LLM的潜在解决方案，以提高整体性能和准确性。

44520292.article_content:
Is Gemini 2.5 good at bounding boxes? Sort of...
July 10, 2025
TL;DR Gemini 2.5 Pro is a decent object detector, matching Yolo V3 from 2018 on MS-COCO val.
Multimodal Large Language Models keep getting better, but are they ready to dethrone CNNs in computer vision tasks like object detection? The allure of skipping dataset collection, annotation, and training is too enticing not to waste a few evenings testing.
I decided to write a small benchmark and check Gemini 2.5 on MS-COCO, focusing on object detection. You can find the code and more results
here
.
Hover or tap to switch between ground truth (green) and Gemini predictions (blue) bounding boxes
Dataset
MS-COCO
is a classic in the object detection world, sure it's a bit dated and the masks/bounding boxes aren't super tight, still, it has a long history and it should be easy to place Gemini among the historical results.
There are 80 classes, from
person
to
toothbrush
. Object boundaries can sometimes be ambiguous, but this tends to even out across the dataset.
The validation set, which you are not supposed to train on, contains 5000 images. However there are no guarantees that Gemini didn't vacuum it up during its training.
COCO sees four cakes, Gemini sees only one
Prompt
I've embedded the list of valid classes from MS-COCO into the prompt, and asked it to follow my JSON output schema. I deliberately avoided explicitly mentioning COCO by name in case Gemini had seen it during training.
Full prompt
Look carefully at this image and detect ALL visible objects, including small ones.
IMPORTANT: Focus on finding as many objects as possible, even if they are small, distant, or partially visible.
Make sure that the bounding box is as tight as possible.
Valid object classes: {class_list}
For each detected object, provide:
-
"label": exact class name from the list above
-
"confidence": how certain you are (0.0 to 1.0)
-
"box_2d": bounding box [ymin, xmin, ymax, xmax] normalized 0-1000
-
"mask": binary mask of the object in the image, as a base64 encoded string
Detect everything you can see that matches the valid classes. Don't be conservative - include objects even if you're only moderately confident.
Return as JSON array:
[
{
"label": "person",
"confidence": 0.95,
"box_2d": [100, 200, 300, 400],
"mask": "..."
},
{
"label": "kite",
"confidence": 0.80,
"box_2d": [50, 150, 250, 350],
"mask": "..."
}
]
Confidence is important for calculating the Average Precision (see Measure section), however, from experience and some sampling the output only partially correlates with better matches.
I ran this prompt with and without structured output, and to burn a bit more credits I also tried both with and without a thinking budget (1024 tokens). For Pro, a thinking budget of *128 tokens is the minimum, I also tried with 2048 tokens. The Gemini documentation recommends to turn it off, and looking at the result that seems like sound advice.
Initially, I wrote 1024 tokens, but it was pointed out that the minimum is in fact 128. I have updated the results table, but it didn't change the overall outcome.
Measure
In object detection, mAP (mean Average Precision) is essentially the average precision of the model's predictions across multiple overlap thresholds (Intersection over Union - IoU), typically ranging from 0.5 to 0.95. Higher values are better. The goal here is to collapse a graph showing how precision changes as recall changes into a single number, since it's much easier to benchmark with a single number.
Here is some pseudo code, not sure if it makes things any clearer, there are also a lot of guides floating around for mAP with nice illustrations:
def
iou
(
box_a
,
box_b
):
return
intersection_area
(
box_a
,
box_b
)
/
union_area
(
box_a
,
box_b
)
def
calculate_ap
(
threshold
):
# Mark predictions as True or False positives based on IoU threshold
for
prediction
in
predictions
:
prediction
.
true_positive
=
iou
(
prediction
,
ground_truth
)
>
threshold
# Sort predictions by confidence (important for the curve!)
predictions
=
sorted
(
predictions
,
key
=
lambda
x
:
x
.
confidence
,
reverse
=
True
)
true_positives
=
0
false_positives
=
0
precision_values
=
[]
recall_values
=
[]
total_ground_truth
=
len
(
ground_truth_objects
)
for
prediction
in
predictions
:
if
prediction
.
true_positive
:
true_positives
+=
1
else
:
false_positives
+=
1
precision
=
true_positives
/
(
true_positives
+
false_positives
)
recall
=
true_positives
/
total_ground_truth
precision_values
.
append
(
precision
)
recall_values
.
append
(
recall
)
# Calculate area under precision-recall curve
return
area_under_curve
(
precision_values
,
recall_values
)
# Finally average over multiple thresholds
mAP
=
sum
(
calculate_ap
(
threshold
)
for
threshold
in
[
0.50
,
0.55
,
...
,
0.95
])
/
10
Results
The results are fairly clear:
Pro is better than Flash, which is better than Flash-Lite.
Adding a thinking budget reduces the performance significantly.

data.title: Automatically Packaging a Haskell Library as a Swift Binary XCFramework
data.author: Bogdanp
data.article_summary:
本文介绍了如何通过`xcframework`将Haskell库集成到Swift应用中，避免直接在XCode中进行复杂的配置。主要内容包括：

1. **XCFrameworks**：Apple在WWDC19推出的多平台二进制框架包，可以通过二进制可链接工件和头文件创建Swift包。
2. **安装xcframework**：在Cabal文件中更改构建类型为Hooks，并添加对`xcframework`的依赖。创建`SetupHooks.hs`文件以自动生成`.xcframework`。
3. **使用XCFramework**：在XCode中添加生成的`.xcframework`到项目设置中，并在Swift代码中导入Haskell的RTS和导出的函数。
4. **示例**：展示了如何在SwiftUI应用中初始化Haskell的RTS，调用Haskell函数，并在应用终止时退出RTS。

通过`xcframework`，开发者可以简化Haskell和Swift的互操作，无需复杂的配置和脚本。

Contents
1
Announcing: xcframework
1.1
XCFrameworks
1.2
How to install
xcframework
1.3
How to use the XCFramework in XCode
1.4
Building simple Swift package
1.5
Must use Cabal Foreign Library stanza
1.6
Conclusion
I’ve written about
Haskell x Swift
interoperability before.
Calling Haskell from Swift
is
about marshalling and the foreign function interface. But
Creating a macOS app
with Haskell and Swift
tells the
much messier tale of hijacking XCode to vodoo together the Haskell library, its
headers, and two handfuls of other magic ingredients into one buildable SwiftUI
application.
Stop! Don’t click on the last link. No, it turns out that my XCode sallies
strayed very far from the yellow brick road. The IDE is confused. Recompilation
bugs abound. Complexity is through the roof juggling
.modulemap
s,
.xcconfig
dynamic settings, and sketchy
.sh
scripts.
Let’s walk the happy path.
1
Announcing: xcframework
Perhaps obvious in retrospect, the
demon-less
way to add a Haskell library to
the dependencies of a Swift application is to build an independent
Swift Package wrapping the Haskell library – something that can be done
without XCode in sight. Easy peasy:
Build the Haskell library using Cabal
Create a Swift package from the Haskell artifacts
Add the Swift package as a dependency to the project
And it turns out that (1) and (2) can be merged together using
Cabal
SetupHooks
!
Moreover, I’m happy to announce I’ve neatly packaged and released that build
process automation as a Haskell library called
xcframework
on Hackage.
Onwards! – for what it does and how to use it.
1.1
XCFrameworks
Apple introduced XCFramework bundles back in a
WWDC19
session
. An XCFramework
is a
multiplatform binary framework bundle
.
For our purposes, that means we can create a Swift Package just from a binary
linkable artifact and a couple of header files. Then, any Swift project can
depend on this binary Swift package and call the functions exposed to the
headers and make sure the bundled library will be linked in with the final
executable. Specifically, the
xcframework
Haskell library, for a given
Haskell library, bundles:
The foreign shared library (
.dylib
) resulting from building with GHC/Cabal
The foreign export headers generated from the
foreign export <haskell_function>
declarations
The RTS headers
which are needed to initialize the RTS from Swift
and because they are
#include
d by the
foreign export
headers
A
.modulemap
exporting the foreign exported functions and
HsFFI.h
The module map basically turns the headers into a Swift module that can
be transparently
import
ed from other Swift modules.
And any Swift library or application can transparently depend on this
.xcframework
and use the foreign exported Haskell functions without further
ado.
1.2
How to install
xcframework
In your cabal file, change the
build-type
to
Hooks
(and set
cabal-version: 3.14
if not set already):
- build-type:     Simple
+ build-type:     Hooks
And add a
setup-depends
stanza with a dependency on
xcframework
:
custom-setup
setup-depends:
base        >= 4.18 && < 5,
xcframework >= 0.1
Finally, create a file called
SetupHooks.hs
in the root of your Cabal package
with the following contents, substituting the
_build/MyHaskellLib.xcframework
string for the
filepath to where the
.xcframework
should be written:
module
SetupHooks
( setupHooks )
where
import
Distribution.XCFramework.SetupHooks
setupHooks ::
SetupHooks
setupHooks
=
xcframeworkHooks
"_build/MyHaskellLib.xcframework"
Now, whenever you run
cabal build
, the built libraries will also be bundled into an
.xcframework
.
1.3
How to use the XCFramework in XCode
In XCode:
Navigate to the target settings of your project.
Find under “General” the “Frameworks, Libraries, and Embedded Content” (or similar) section.
Click the add button and add the
.xcframework
framework outputted at the specified path by Cabal
Now, in the entry Swift module, import the RTS and init/exit the RTS. For
instance, in a sample SwiftUI app:
import SwiftUI
+ import Haskell.Foreign.Rts
@main
struct MyExample: App {
+
+     init() {
+         hs_init(nil, nil)
+
+         NotificationCenter.default
+           .addObserver(forName: NSApplication.willTerminateNotification,
+                        object: nil, queue: .main) { _ in
+           hs_exit()
+         }
+     }
+
var body: some Scene {
WindowGroup {
ContentView()
}
}
}
Finally, in any Swift module, do
import Haskell.Foreign.Exports
. For now, the
name
Haskell.Foreign.Exports
is fixed and exports all foreign-exported
functions, but it could be improved in the future (perhaps it’s a good task to
contribute a patch for!)
For example, if your Haskell module looked like:
module
MyLib
(doSomething)
where
fib ::
Integral
b
=>
Int
->
b
fib n
=
round
$
phi
**
fromIntegral
n
/
sq5
where
sq5
=
sqrt
5
::
Double
phi
=
(
1
+
sq5)
/
2
doSomething ::
IO
Int
doSomething
=
do
putStrLn
"doing some thing"
return
$
fib
42
foreign export ccall
doSomething ::
IO
Int

data.title: Flix – A powerful effect-oriented programming language
data.author: freilanzer
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Flix 语言的特性、优点、缺点以及与其他语言和生态系统（如JVM、Haskell、Scala等）的比较。

不同观点：
• **Flix 的优点和独特性**：exceptione 对 Flix 语言的代数数据类型、逻辑编程、可变性等特性印象深刻，尤其赞赏其单个可执行文件集成了包管理器、语言服务器协议（LSP）和编译器。他还提到 Flix 在与 JVM 生态系统（如 Java）集成方面的潜力，尽管存在类型擦除问题，但通过 "regions" 概念支持命令式交互。

• **记录的多态性语义**：Joker_vD 关注 Flix 的记录扩展和限制的多态性语义，认为其遵循 Leijen 的方法，允许记录字段的重加和移除，且行为合理。相比之下，早期尝试通过复杂的类型系统静态禁止这种行为显得不必要。

• **语法问题**：daxfohl 对 Flix 语法中的分号使用提出批评，特别是在 `yield` 示例中，最后一行没有 "return" 导致不对称感。他表示可以接受大括号或缩进，但分号必须去掉。

• **Flix 与 Java 的比较和教学**：lutzh 提到曾写过一篇 "Flix for Java Programmers" 的文章，认为 Flix 对于 Java 程序员来说非常有趣，但需要更新以反映 Flix 的最新发展。

• **Aarhus 作为编程语言研究重镇的原因**：textlapse 提出一个题外问题，探讨丹麦奥胡斯大学/科技中心为何成为编程语言研究的强大中心，涉及 C++、C#、Typescript、Dart 等语言的根源。

• **类型类和宏的支持**：pshirshov 关注 Flix 是否支持高阶类型（HKTs）和类型类（在 Flix 中称为 traits）。他对缺乏标称继承表示失望，认为这使得某些有用的抽象无法实现或变得丑陋。

• **代码智能工具的支持**：daxfohl 幽默地提到，是否需要依赖代码智能工具，还是需要自己动脑。同时担心 LLMs 可能会抑制新语言的采用。

• **对 Flix 的兴趣和使用意愿**：andoando 表达了对 Flix 的喜爱，这是他第一次看到新编程语言演示后产生使用欲望。voat 则表示尽管 Flix 看起来很美，但自己是 Web 开发者，从不接触 JVM 生态系统。

• **效果导向编程的介绍需求**：mcdow 请求关于效果导向编程的具体介绍和使用示例。

• **与其他语言的比较**：syhol 指出 Flix 与 Koka 语言非常相似，并希望这些效果系统能够成为主流。Hashex129542 则简单地表示不喜欢过多的关键字。

• **模式匹配的语法建议**：pmontra 对比了 Flix 和 Elixir 的模式匹配语法，建议 Flix 可以更简洁、更 DRY（不重复自己），并提出结构化模式匹配的概念。

• **查询语法的顺序问题**：naasking 对 Flix 查询语句中 `select` 的位置提出异议，认为应该像 LINQ 那样将 `select` 放在最后，以避免 SQL 中的问题。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及的 Flix 文档和外部资源链接（如 lutzh 的文章、Flix 官方文档中的 JVM 互操作性说明）为深入了解 Flix 提供了参考。
• 对 LLMs 可能抑制新语言采用的担忧，以及对编程语言设计中语法和语义的细节讨论，也体现了开发者社区对语言易用性和生产力的关注。

• **Aarhus 作为编程语言研究重镇的原因**：textlapse 提出一个题外问题，探讨丹麦奥胡斯大学/科技中心为何成为编程语言研究的强大中心，涉及 C++、C#、Typescript、Dart 等语言的根源。

• **类型类和宏的支持**：pshirshov 关注 Flix 是否支持高阶类型（HKTs）和类型类（在 Flix 中称为 traits）。他对缺乏标称继承表示失望，认为这使得某些有用的抽象无法实现或变得丑陋。

• **代码智能工具的支持**：daxfohl 幽默地提到，是否需要依赖代码智能工具，还是需要自己动脑。同时担心 LLMs 可能会抑制新语言的采用。

• **对 Flix 的兴趣和使用意愿**：andoando 表达了对 Flix 的喜爱，这是他第一次看到新编程语言演示后产生使用欲望。voat 则表示尽管 Flix 看起来很美，但自己是 Web 开发者，从不接触 JVM 生态系统。

• **效果导向编程的介绍需求**：mcdow 请求关于效果导向编程的具体介绍和使用示例。

• **与其他语言的比较**：syhol 指出 Flix 与 Koka 语言非常相似，并希望这些效果系统能够成为主流。Hashex129542 则简单地表示不喜欢过多的关键字。

• **模式匹配的语法建议**：pmontra 对比了 Flix 和 Elixir 的模式匹配语法，建议 Flix 可以更简洁、更 DRY（不重复自己），并提出结构化模式匹配的概念。

• **查询语法的顺序问题**：naasking 对 Flix 查询语句中 `select` 的位置提出异议，认为应该像 LINQ 那样将 `select` 放在最后，以避免 SQL 中的问题。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及的 Flix 文档和外部资源链接（如 lutzh 的文章、Flix 官方文档中的 JVM 互操作性说明）为深入了解 Flix 提供了参考。
• 对 LLMs 可能抑制新语言采用的担忧，以及对编程语言设计中语法和语义的细节讨论，也体现了开发者社区对语言易用性和生产力的关注。

Exhibitions
news
Executed Chinese prisoners likely used in UK exhibition
Cadavers on display in 'Real Bodies' show were provided by Dalian-based firm known to have acquired corpses from police
Cristina Ruiz
25 January 2021
Share
The bodies in the exhibition have been stripped of their skin and dissected to reveal their internal anatomy
© jacquemart
An exhibition of preserved human corpses in Birmingham may have included political prisoners executed in China, according to British parliamentarians.
Speaking in the House of Lords on 12 January, Lord Alton of Liverpool said that the cadavers used in an international touring show called Real Bodies, which was seen at the National Exhibition Centre in Birmingham in 2018, “were probably people who had been executed” in China.
The bodies on display were stripped of their skin, dissected to show a part of their internal anatomy and then infused with plastic, which gradually hardened, a process known as plastination.
They were obtained from a firm in Dalian, China which has used corpses acquired from the Chinese police, according to a previous investigation by the New York Attorney General’s Office.
The exhibition was discussed during a debate on a proposed amendment to a new British law which is currently under consideration, the Medicines and Medical Devices Bill. The amendment would require all human tissues and cells imported into Britain for medical or scientific purposes to be fully documented with evidence that they were obtained with the consent of the donor.
The amendment is the first legislative response in Britain to the findings of the China Tribunal, an independent panel set up in London to investigate evidence that the Chinese state is removing organs from prisoners while they are still alive as part of a lucrative black-market trade in organ transplants.
Real Bodies: The Exhibition travelled to the South Florida Science Center and Aquarium in 2020
© Photo by Damon Higgins/USA Today Network/Sipa USA.
In June 2019, the tribunal concluded that “forced organ harvesting has been committed for years throughout China on a significant scale” and that “Falun Gong practitioners have been one—and probably the main—source of organ supply”, adding that evidence of forced organ harvesting of the persecuted Uyghur population may yet emerge.
“It is extraordinary that such things can happen in the 21st century, but they are happening,” Lord Alton told the House of Lords on 12 January. “It is crucial that we discover the origins of the bodies that are used in these sorts of exhibitions, which I personally believe should be prohibited in their entirety. The idea that they can be paraded for macabre purposes should fill people with a sense of disgust.”
Real Bodies
is organised by Imagine Exhibitions, a US firm based in Atlanta, Georgia. According to the firm’s website, the show has “recently been updated with the latest scientific research on how Covid-19 impacts the human body”. It is available for hire internationally as a pre-packaged show.
The company did not respond to a request for comment.
However, in an earlier debate in the House of Lords last October, Lord Alton noted that “in 2018, we pointed out that the US organisers, Imagine Exhibitions, were unable to provide any evidence of consent for the use of these cadavers. The organisers merely said that the cadavers were unclaimed bodies obtained from Dalian Hoffen Bio-Technique Company China. Imagine Exhibitions CEO, Tom Zaller, admitted in an interview that the bodies were ‘absolutely from China’ but added that there was ‘no documentation’ to prove their identities or to show they had agreed in life to donate their corpses in death.”
According to Imagine Exhibitions’ website, from 1999 to 2009 Zaller worked at Premier Exhibitions, another US firm which organised touring shows of plastinated bodies. In 2008, the then Attorney General of New York, Andrew Cuomo, reached a settlement with Premier which “brings an end to Premier’s practice of using bodies of undocumented origins in their exhibitions”, according to a press release issued on 29 May 2008. For future shows in the state, the company would be required to “obtain documentation demonstrating the cause of death and origins of the cadavers and body parts it displays as well as proof that the decedent consented to the use of his or her remains in such a manner”.
The press release noted that all of the corpses included in a version of the show then on display at New York City’s South Street Seaport were licensed by Premier Exhibitions from the Dalian Hoffen Bio-Technique Company which, in turn, had “acquired [them] indirectly from the Chinese Bureau of Police”. The company was, the press release continued, “unable to demonstrate the cause of death or the origin of the decedents”.

← Back to Home
← Back to Writings
The Only SaaS Feature You Should Be Building
7/9/2025
“SaaS is dead. The future is CRUD apps that act as a thin layer over data. The real work will happen through agents that interact with both data and people.”
– Satya Nadella (paraphrased)
I believe Satya is
generally
correct here. But before companies can get there, they have to solve one critical piece:
the action interface for human operators
.
This is a necessary step before the coming wave of headless AI. I’ll post about that next.
Why the Action Interface Matters
AI infrastructure and agentic layers are moving quickly. There’s progress on semantic layers, orchestration engines, eval frameworks, all great for admins and technical users. But what about the operators? The people actually running day-to-day workflows?
Here’s the truth: most operators aren’t prompt engineers. They don’t have time to fine-tune context, build evals, or craft perfect instructions. Their job is to keep the world moving, keep making the widgets.
What they need is simple:
A clean interface that let’s them
react to and confirm actions.
A way to
proactively ask the system to take actions.
Yet SaaS companies are still building AI for a rare technical user.
The Two Modes of Work
Almost all SaaS tools today boil down to two patterns:
Tasks/queues —
where operators work through a list
Proactive actions —
where operators drive work forward (e.g. scheduling, updating records)
Everything else (alerts, dashboards, comments) is either feeding into or enabling those two modes.We’ve seen a lot of focus on proactive UX: chat interfaces, canvases, dynamic UIs. That’s important. But what’s missing, what every SaaS company will need to nail, is the reactive side. That’s where the next big unlock lies: designing interfaces that let operators react without friction.
The New Paradigm: Reactive Agentic UX
Reactive UX means operators aren’t hunting around for what to do. They’re not juggling five separate interfaces. They react to actions and insights. They have a single, go-to agentic interface. The agent surfaces the right actions at the right time. The Operator Interface is where the work gets done:
Reviews, confirms, or adjusts what the agent proposes
Creates the building block for real-world (logistics, support, field service, deskless worforce, etc.), human-in-the-loop training
To work in heavy operations, this interface can’t just be a static list. It needs a few critical components:
It should support intelligent task queueing and routing, automatically assigning tasks to the right user or team with clear prioritization and status indicators like “new,” “in progress,” or “completed.” It should also alert operators when something actually requires their attention, eliminating guesswork or manual triage.
Next, it needs a robust context panel that consolidates all relevant metadata in a single view. Whether it’s order details, historical activity, agent recommendations, or chain-of-thought reasoning, operators should not have to jump between systems just to understand what is happening.
Action controls should be seamless. Operators need one-click confirmations or edits of agent suggestions, along with the ability to reject or override them when necessary. Every action should be recorded with an audit trail so there is never ambiguity about what was done, who did it, or why.
Collaboration must also be built in. That includes simple hand-off or escalation flows for edge cases, as well as lightweight commenting or tagging so other team members can contribute without disrupting the workflow.
Finally, the interface should empower operators to initiate agent actions directly. With predefined templates or smart buttons, they should be able to trigger common workflows like rescheduling a delivery or generating a new quote without having to write a prompt from scratch.In other words, a great Operator Interface surfaces the right actions automatically, provides clear and contextual information, enables operators to react in seconds rather than minutes, and maintains a clean record of everything that happened.
This is the bridge between CRUD apps and true agentic workflows.
What’s Next
If you’re building SaaS or agentic software today, this is the feature to focus on.
Build the operator action interface
Make it dead simple for operators to engage with agents… No prompts, no context-building, no friction.
Headless AI is coming. But this is the bridge we have to build first.

data.title: Koala: A benchmark suite for performance-oriented shell-optimization research
data.author: matt_d
data.article_summary:
Koala是一个面向性能优化的基准测试套件，包含14组来自不同领域的真实壳程序，如CI/CD、AI/ML、生物学和人文学科，并附带真实输入数据，支持大规模和小规模的性能测试。主要目录包括：  
- **analytics**: 处理网络日志  
- **bio**: 基因组和转录组分析  
- **ci-cd**: 构建和测试开源软件  
- **covid**: 分析疫情期间公共交通  
- **file-mod**: 文件压缩、加密和格式转换  
- **inference**: 使用大型模型进行媒体推理  
- **ml**: 实现机器学习管道  
- **nlp**: 使用壳NLP管道处理书籍  
- **oneliners**: 执行经典和现代壳管道  
- **pkg**: 构建AUR包并分析npm权限  
- **repl**: 安全审计和Git工作流重放  
- **unixfun**: 解决Unix文本处理问题  
- **weather**: 计算和可视化历史天气  
- **web-search**: 爬取和索引Wikipedia数据  

Koala提供了快速设置指南，可以通过脚本、克隆仓库或Docker获取，并使用MIT许可证。贡献者可通过GitHub提交问题和想法。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：是否应该使用Bash编写脚本，尤其是在性能可能成为瓶颈的情况下

不同观点：
• [meisel的观点] 认为如果脚本的性能已经到达Shell可能是瓶颈的程度，那么就不应该继续使用Bash编写，而应该选择更合适的编程语言。这暗示Bash在处理复杂或高性能任务时不够理想，应该选用更强大的编程语言来处理这些任务。

• [反驳观点] 有些人可能认为Bash在快速原型设计和处理简单任务时非常高效，尤其是对于系统管理员或需要快速执行的小型脚本。即便性能存在瓶颈，也可以通过优化代码或使用其他工具来缓解，而不一定必须切换语言。

• [中立观点] 另一部分人可能认为选择编程语言应根据具体场景决定。如果Bash已经能满足大部分需求，只是某些部分存在性能问题，可以通过混合编程的方式解决，即用Bash处理简单逻辑，而用C、Python等其他语言处理性能关键部分。

补充讨论：
• Bash的优势在于其简洁和与系统工具的高度集成，适合快速执行系统任务和管理脚本。
• 切换语言会带来额外的学习成本和复杂性，尤其对那些主要工作不是编程的系统管理员或DevOps人员。
• 争议的焦点在于是否应该为了性能问题完全放弃Bash，还是通过其他方式优化或混合编程来解决问题。

Koala is a benchmark suite aimed at the characterization of performance-oriented research targeting the POSIX shell.
It consists of 14 sets of real-world shell programs from diverse domains ranging from CI/CD and AI/ML to biology and the humanities. They are accompanied by real inputs that facilitate small- and large-scale performance characterization and varying opportunities for optimization.

Benchmarks

Benchmark
Description
analytics
processes real-world network logs to extract and summarize key events.
bio
performs genomic and transcriptomic analysis using population and RNA-seq data.
ci-cd
builds and tests open-source software projects.
covid
analyzes public transit activity during the covid-19 pandemic.
file-mod
compresses, encrypts, and converts various file formats.
inference
runs media-related inference tasks using large foundation models.
ml
implements a full machine learning pipeline using scikit-learn.
nlp
processes books using shell-based nlp pipelines from unix for poets.
oneliners
executes classic and modern one-liner shell pipelines.
pkg
builds aur packages and analyzes npm packages for permissions.
repl
performs security auditing and git-based development workflow replay.
unixfun
solves unix text-processing problems from the 50-year anniversary challenge.
weather
computes and visualizes historical weather statistics.
web-search
implements crawling, indexing, and querying of wikipedia data.

- **bio**: 基因组和转录组分析  
- **ci-cd**: 构建和测试开源软件  
- **covid**: 分析疫情期间公共交通  
- **file-mod**: 文件压缩、加密和格式转换  
- **inference**: 使用大型模型进行媒体推理  
- **ml**: 实现机器学习管道  
- **nlp**: 使用壳NLP管道处理书籍  
- **oneliners**: 执行经典和现代壳管道  
- **pkg**: 构建AUR包并分析npm权限  
- **repl**: 安全审计和Git工作流重放  
- **unixfun**: 解决Unix文本处理问题  
- **weather**: 计算和可视化历史天气  
- **web-search**: 爬取和索引Wikipedia数据  

Koala提供了快速设置指南，可以通过脚本、克隆仓库或Docker获取，并使用MIT许可证。贡献者可通过GitHub提交问题和想法。

data.title: Could a Paper Plane Thrown from the ISS Survive the Flight?
data.author: dxs
data.article_summary: 文章探讨了从国际空间站投掷纸飞机的可能性及其飞行 dynamics。作者Maximilien Berthet和Kojiro Suzuki通过软件模拟和风洞实验研究了纸飞机从400公里高度（ISS轨道高度）以7800米/秒速度投掷后的表现。模拟显示，纸飞机在前3.5天能保持稳定，但由于低弹道系数，下降至120公里高度时，因空气密度增加而失控翻滚。风洞实验中，纸飞机在承受7秒高超音速风（马赫7）后，虽然机头弯曲并出现烧焦迹象，但未解体。实验证明纸飞机无法完整返回地面，但这种设计启发未来可用于如金星探测等任务中的一次性探测器。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：纸飞机从低地球轨道（LEO）再入大气层时的行为和物理特性

不同观点：
• **nickparker**：认为文章没有覆盖实际结论，强调了模拟与实验研究的主要发现，包括轨道衰减速度、姿态稳定性以及再入大气层时的严重加热问题，可能导致燃烧或热解。
• **peterlk**：同意纸飞机很可能在大气层中燃烧，引用了原始论文支持这个观点。
• **ngriffiths**：质疑文章没有明确说明纸飞机从放置到开始下降的过程，强调了纸飞机由于低弹道系数快速脱轨的特点，并与国际空间站（ISS）的轨道衰减做了对比。
• **fainpul**：认为风洞测试条件与实际大气条件有很大不同，提出纸飞机质量小，可能无法产生足够的热量导致严重加热，并认为即使纸飞机开始翻滚，也可能在低空恢复稳定。
• **FiatLuxDave**：通过计算纸飞机的初始动能和预期加热功率，质疑加热效应的合理性。
• **K0balt**：提出是否存在能够承受这些温度的纸张处理方法或类似材料，比如泡沫隔热材料，但指出这类材料缺少纸飞机的浪漫吸引力。
• **wrp**：直观上认为轻物体由于大帆面积不会经历明显的摩擦加热，质疑纸飞机燃烧的可能性。
• **chris_va**：通过计算黑体辐射功率，指出纸飞机材料无法承受高温，但可能玻璃等材料可以。
• **deadbabe**：提出一个极端假设，使用250英里的电线从地球同步轨道下降，讨论其可行性和摩擦熔化问题。
• **nodesocket**：通过与ChatGPT的后续对话，指出如果飞机由铜或钛制成，由于表面积与质量比不同，其轨道寿命和再入表现会显著不同，强调了弹道系数的关键作用。
• **mcphage**：提出纸直升机的概念，认为它可能比纸飞机更稳定，因为纸直升机会自发旋转。

• 不同材料（如铜、钛）的飞机再入表现引发讨论，强调了弹道系数对轨道寿命的影响。
• 提出了纸直升机作为另一种设计方案，可能具有更好的稳定性。

44521094.article_content:
Could a Paper Plane Thrown From The International Space Station Survive The Flight?
Space
10 July 2025
By
Andy Tomaswick, Universe Today
(kieferpix/Getty Images)
Sometimes there are profound questions in life that must be answered, like "What is the meaning of existence?", "Are we alone in the universe?" or "What happens if you throw a paper airplane from the International Space Station?"
Luckily, that third one has finally been answered, because of course someone would eventually.
A new paper
from Maximilien Berthet and Kojiro Suzuki from the University of Tokyo looks at "the dynamics of an origami space plane during Earth atmospheric reentry"
–
in other words, what happens when you throw a paper plane out of the ISS.
First, let's go over some technical ideas that are necessary to understanding this seemingly simple concept.
Related:
ESA Report Says There's Too Much Junk in Earth Orbit Trunk
Origami literally means folded paper in Japanese, and in this case the authors decided to make their paper airplane out of a standard A4 sheet of white paper. The end result looks like something a third grader would have made up to annoy their friend sitting in front of them in class, but with a lot more aerodynamic modeling.
Once the software model was made, it was time to put it to the test. The ISS orbits at around 400 kilometers (about 250 miles), so the authors decided to launch the plane from that height, and at a speed similar to that of the ISS itself - 7800 meters/second.
That speed might seem likely it would shred any plane made out of paper, but at 400 km altitude the atmosphere isn't thick enough to do much damage… yet.
That's actually the case for the majority of the descent back to the ground. From 400 km down to around 120 km altitude, the plane stays relatively stable, given the lack of air.
However, the plane descends very quickly due to its low ballistic coefficient, which is a measure of how well it can overcome air resistance. With its low ballistic coefficient, the plane rapidly slow, descending to 120 km in about 3.5 days.
On the slip side, a low ballistic coefficient would mean that, once the plane entered the atmosphere it would actually have a lower terminal velocity than something like a cannonball.
Illustration of a paper airplane, thrown from orbit. (NASA/ESA/M. Berthet & K Suzuki)
Unfortunately it never makes it that far, as, according to the simulations, at around 120 km altitude, the increased air density induces uncontrollable tumbling, essentially sending the plane into an uncontrollable flight path familiar to anyone who has ever made one of them.
But why stop at simulations when you have a PhD in Aerospace Engineering and can build a paper airplane for science? And why just build one when you can test one in a hyper-advanced wind tunnel on your university's campus?
The answer is you don't stop - which is why the authors built an actual paper airplane model (admittedly with an aluminum tail) and put it into the Kashiwa Hypersonic and High Enthalpy Wind Tunnel at the University of Tokyo to see what kind of aerodynamic forces their paper airplane could withstand.
They didn't go easy on their experiments either. Their one-third model paper airplane was subjected to Mach 7 winds for 7 seconds, similar to the forces experienced during actual reentry. This, unsurprisingly, bent the nose of the paper airplane back, but to its credit it didn't disintegrate – at least not in that amount of time.
There was also noticeable evidence of charring on the nose and wing tips, indicating that, if the experiment had gone on longer, the paper plane would have burnt up.
Ultimately, proving that's what would happen was one of the purposes of this experiment. There are plenty of mission architectures that could potentially use something similar to this paper airplane model – the LEAVES experiment for
Venus
exploration comes to mind, but there are also plenty of Earth observations that would benefit from a lightweight, stable platform to do their collecting from while burning up completely in the atmosphere at their end of life.
Mounting any such mission would require electronics and many other additions that would complicate the purity of testing a simple paper plane that a kid could have made it class.
But sometimes science is as much about inspiration as it is about exploration, and the results in this paper provide a nice mix of both.

data.title: Where can I see Hokusai's Great Wave today?
data.author: colinprince
data.article_summary: 葛饰北斋的著名作品《神奈川冲浪里》目前在意大利的特雷维索Musei Civici博物馆和南特的历史博物馆展出，分别展至2025年9月28日和2025年9月7日。此外，该作品也在特里este的东方艺术市民博物馆和维罗纳的Palazzo Maffei博物馆展出（信息来自Instagram）。在美国，康涅狄格州的Hill-Stead博物馆也有展出（详见其官网）。还有55个地点也展出该作品。文章还提到可通过GitHub让博物馆或画廊列出展览信息，并可通过RSS订阅更新。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕《神奈川冲浪里》（The Great Wave）及其相关艺术作品的讨论，涉及艺术作品的展示、复制及其文化意义。

不同观点：
• msephton：作为网站的创建者，提到该网站已变得更加自动化，并扩展到搜索新闻稿以获取相关信息。他还提到当前在东京成田机场的数字展览，并指出该作品的持续受欢迎程度。
• akkartik：分享了一个关于如何防止艺术品褪色的链接，并对该技术表现出兴趣。
• esperent：承认《Great Wave》的著名地位，但建议人们去探索葛饰北斋的其他作品，如《瀑布 penitence》和一些更怪异的艺术作品，并提到这些作品对理解现代日本漫画的启示。
• sharkjacobs：质疑观看原作相对于观看高质量复制品的优势，认为原作的重要性可能会影响观众的接受心态，但这也是博物馆和画廊展示策略的一部分。
• mNovak：推荐David Bull的YouTube频道作为了解这些版画及其历史的资源，并提到《Great Wave》在葛饰北斋生前已被广泛复制，因此很难确定某个印本是否为“原作”。
• OPBoot：建议支持像David Bull这样的当代艺术家，他们在努力保持传统日本木版画艺术的活力，并提供购买《Great Wave》复制品的链接。
• fusslo：分享了自己在康涅狄格州的成长经历，提到对当地艺术博物馆的新发现和未能及早体验的遗憾。
• aosaigh：对著名艺术品的临时展览运作方式提出疑问，包括博物馆是否支付原作拥有者以展出作品，以及运输的昂贵成本。
• seafoamteal：提到通过阅读小说《Tomorrow and Tomorrow and Tomorrow》了解到《Great Wave》，该作品在书中起到一定作用。
• poulpy123：解释了《Great Wave》可以在两个博物馆同时展出的原因是因为存在约100份印刷品。
• xnx：分享了Google艺术与文化的链接，提供对《Great Wave》的在线查看。
• amarcheschi：提到亲眼见到《Great Wave》时对其小尺寸感到意外，认为其被称为“伟大”提高了期望值。
• burnt-resistor：回忆起《Great Wave》曾被用作《Applications of Digital Signal Processing to Audio and Acoustics》一书的封面，并误记其出现在90年代的高中AP微积分教材上。
• ChrisMarshallNY：提到《Great Wave》让他想起了“Is Abe Vigoda Dead?”网站，这是一种对持续在线状态的幽默类比。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点：对原作与复制品的价值讨论，特别是原作的重要性是否仅仅因为其“重要”地位而影响观众体验。
• 其他值得注意的讨论点：对艺术品运输和展览运作方式的疑问，以及对《Great Wave》文化影响的个人回忆和联想。

主要讨论点：AI编码工具的实际效果和使用体验

不同观点：
• **[jtc-hn的观点]**：认为AI工具（特别是类型预估工具）常常引入细微错误或不准确的函数名称，导致用户浪费时间去评估或修正AI的建议。这些工具虽然有帮助，但缺乏足够的上下文理解，可能会在代码的某一处做出修改，却导致其他部分出现问题，需要大量人工管理，打断了编码的流畅性。
  
• **[duxup的观点]**：对AI工具持较为积极的态度。虽然承认AI的建议并非总是完全准确，但认为通过主动探索和调查AI的建议，可以提升代码质量。同时认为，谨慎使用AI工具并主动承担责任是合理的做法。

• **[mertleee的观点]**：对AI工具的效果感到困惑，提到自己可能因为依赖工具而忘记了某些技术面试中需要的简写技巧，不确定是自己能力问题还是工具的实际效用。

补充讨论：
• **AI工具的上下文理解不足**：jtc-hn指出当前AI工具在处理代码时，缺乏对整体项目的上下文理解，导致需要人为干预。
• **AI工具对编码流畅性的影响**：jtc-hn提到AI工具的错误建议会打断编码思路，增加额外的工作量。
• **主动探索与责任承担**：duxup强调使用AI工具时，主动调查和验证其建议是负责任的做法，并认为这可能带来更好的代码质量。
• **依赖AI工具的副作用**：mertleee担心过度依赖AI工具可能导致自身技能的退化，特别是在技术面试等场景中。

争议焦点：
• AI工具是否真的提高了编码效率和质量，还是反而增加了额外的工作量和管理成本。
• 过度依赖AI工具是否会导致程序员自身技能的退化。

总结：讨论主要围绕AI编码工具的优缺点展开，涉及其对编码效率、代码质量以及程序员自身技能的影响。不同用户对工具的实际效果有不同的体验和看法。

主要讨论点：咖啡价格上涨的原因及影响

不同观点：
• anenefan：认为咖啡价格上涨是由于批发价格上升和投机行为导致的。他们指出期货市场本应提供产品稳定性和可获得性，但往往导致与大贸易集团有合约的农民陷入困境，因为这些集团即使在较低利润下仍能获利。
    └ 支持论据：引用了2024年关于巴西咖啡产业受现实冲击的文章，以及2024年9月关于自然灾害导致作物减产的新闻。

• alexk307：认为气候变化是咖啡价格上涨的唯一原因，并指出未来情况可能会更糟。他们引用了一系列新闻文章来支持这一观点。
    └ 支持论据：
        - 引用NBC新闻关于消费者面临的咖啡成本上升的文章。
        - 引用Inc.com关于 Associated Press 报道的咖啡价格上涨新闻。
        - 引用纽约时报关于咖啡价格的文章。
        - 引用Sopris Sun关于专家对咖啡价格上涨的分析。

• amelius：对投机行为能创造流动性和提高市场效率的说法持怀疑态度，并幽默地表示不介意偶尔反驳这种说法，但不要触及他们的咖啡。
    └ 支持论据：提供了一个存档链接，暗示对投机行为导致市场效率提高的说法不以为然。

• 争议焦点：咖啡价格上涨的主要原因。anenefan强调投机和期货市场对农民的影响，而alexk307则将责任完全归咎于气候变化。
• amelius的观点则更侧重于对市场投机行为的批评，虽然没有直接参与气候变化的讨论，但通过幽默方式表达了对市场运作方式的不满。

data.title: Libpostal: C library for parsing/normalizing street addresses around the world
data.author: nateb2022
data.article_summary: libpostal是一个开源的C语言库，用于解析和规范化全球街道地址。它利用统计自然语言处理（NLP）和开放地理数据，帮助将人类使用的非结构化地址转换为适合机器比较和全文索引的规范化形式。该库支持多种语言，并提供Python、Ruby、Go、Java、PHP和NodeJS的官方语言绑定。虽然libpostal本身不是完整的地理编码器，但可以作为预处理步骤，提高国际地理编码应用的智能性、简化性和一致性。安装过程包括在Mac和Linux系统上通过不同包管理器安装依赖并编译库。项目依赖赞助以持续发展地理空间NLP研究。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：地址解析和标准化库（如libpostal）的应用及其局限性

不同观点：
• [支持观点] 一些用户认为libpostal是一个强大且有用的库，能够在处理全球地址解析时提供良好性能，优于正则表达式，并且在多个项目中取得了成功。例如，[Ameo]和[alganet]提到libpostal在解析地址时表现出色，能够有效处理许多极端情况，且易于集成到不同语言的项目中。

• [质疑观点] 部分用户对地址解析库的有效性提出质疑，认为地址本质上是无结构的数据，无法通过解析或标准化来验证其有效性。例如，[kerkeslager]认为，唯一可靠的验证方法是将地址与全球地址数据集进行对比，而不是依赖解析库。此外，[shakna]通过分享自己在非正式地址系统中的实际经历，说明了在某些地区地址的非标准化程度极高，解析库可能无法处理。

• [技术细节和挑战] 一些用户讨论了地址解析的技术挑战和系统要求。例如，[jandrese]指出全球地址格式和惯例的多样性使得地址验证成为一个几乎无法解决的问题。同时，[claytongulick]提到libpostal虽然功能强大，但并非轻量级工具，需要大量的存储空间和运行时资源。

• [替代方案] 部分用户提到使用商业服务或其它库来进行地址和电话号码的验证与标准化。例如，[weinzierl]提到Google的libphonenumber库，并指出许多公司使用商业服务来处理这些任务。

补充讨论：
• 一些用户分享了他们在实际项目中使用地址解析库的经验和挑战，例如[ttw44]在初学Web开发时遇到的困难，以及[RobinL]对libpostal在特定应用（如地址匹配）中局限性的分析。

• 还有用户提到相关项目和工具，如[gorgoiler]列举了一些用于处理日常事物的编码工具，显示出对这类工具的广泛兴趣。

争议焦点：
• 地址解析库（如libpostal）在处理全球多样化地址格式时的有效性和实用性，以及是否存在更好的替代方案（如基于全球地址数据集的搜索引擎）。

libpostal: international street address NLP
libpostal is a C library for parsing/normalizing street addresses around the world using statistical NLP and open data. The goal of this project is to understand location-based strings in every language, everywhere. For a more comprehensive overview of the research behind libpostal, be sure to check out the (lengthy) introductory blog posts:
Original post
:
Statistical NLP on OpenStreetMap
Follow-up for 1.0 release
:
Statistical NLP on OpenStreetMap: Part 2

Addresses and the locations they represent are essential for any application dealing with maps (place search, transportation, on-demand/delivery services, check-ins, reviews). Yet even the simplest addresses are packed with local conventions, abbreviations and context, making them difficult to index/query effectively with traditional full-text search engines. This library helps convert the free-form addresses that humans use into clean normalized forms suitable for machine comparison and full-text indexing. Though libpostal is not itself a full geocoder, it can be used as a preprocessing step to make any geocoding application smarter, simpler, and more consistent internationally.

The core library is written in pure C. Language bindings for
Python
,
Ruby
,
Go
,
Java
,
PHP
, and
NodeJS
are officially supported and it's easy to write bindings in other languages.
Sponsors
If your company is using libpostal, consider asking your organization to sponsor the project. Interpreting what humans mean when they refer to locations is far from a solved problem, and sponsorships help us pursue new frontiers in geospatial NLP. As a sponsor, your company logo will appear prominently on the Github repo page along with a link to your site.
Sponsorship info
Backers
Individual users can also help support open geo NLP research by making a monthly donation:
Installation (Mac/Linux)
Before you install, make sure you have the following prerequisites:
On Ubuntu/Debian
sudo apt-get install -y curl build-essential autoconf automake libtool pkg-config
On CentOS/RHEL
sudo yum install curl autoconf automake libtool pkgconfig
On macOS
Install with one command via
MacPorts
:
port install libpostal
Or as follows with
Homebrew
:
brew install curl autoconf automake libtool pkg-config
Then to install the C library:
If you're using an M1 Mac, add
--disable-sse2
to the
./configure
command. This will result in poorer performance but the build will succeed.
git clone https://github.com/openvenues/libpostal
cd libpostal
# skip if installing for the first time
make distclean
./bootstrap.sh
# omit --datadir flag to install data in current directory
./configure --datadir=[...some dir with a few GB of space where a "libpostal" directory exists or can be created/modified...]
make -j4
# For Intel/AMD processors and the default model
./configure --datadir=[...some dir with a few GB of space where a "libpostal" directory exists or can be created/modified...]
# For Apple / ARM cpus and the default model
./configure --datadir=[...some dir with a few GB of space where a "libpostal" directory exists or can be created/modified...] --disable-sse2
# For the improved Senzing model:
./configure --datadir=[...some dir with a few GB of space where a "libpostal" directory exists or can be created/modified...] MODEL=senzing
make -j8
sudo make install
# On Linux it's probably a good idea to run
sudo ldconfig
libpostal has support for pkg-config, so you can use the pkg-config to print the flags needed to link your program against it:
pkg-config --cflags libpostal         # print compiler flags
pkg-config --libs libpostal           # print linker flags
pkg-config --cflags --l
